title: A drawing can use fonts the user provides
body:
acre embeds its fonts in `crates/acre/src/render.rs`: JetBrains Mono, Noto Sans in three faces, and, after the math issue, a math font. `font` takes one of the names `mono`, `sans`, `sans-bold`, `sans-italic`.

## Proposal

- A canvas-level `fonts { name "path/to/font.ttf"; ... }` registers font files under names that `font` then accepts. A program crate reads the files and passes their bytes to the library, which still reads no file itself.
- The math font can be swapped the same way, provided it has a MATH table.
close_reason: Landed on dev in 35ad092: a canvas `fonts` node registers font files under names `font` accepts, and `math` in it swaps the math font (MATH table required). acre-cli and acre-gui read the files; the library takes bytes. Syntax choices are a note on acre-4518a5.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/ed2a7ee0
notes.text: Landed. The library reports files through scene::font_files(&Program) -> Vec<FontFile{name,path,span}> and scene::build(&Program, &[Vec<u8>]) takes the bytes in that order. A Fonts value (src/fonts.rs, Arc inside) holds each file's bytes with its parsed face via self_cell, and is carried by Scene, by Label and by Code, because text::layout is called from draw code with no scene in hand. Font::Custom(u16) indexes the registered fonts. Dead end avoided: leaking bytes to get 'static faces would grow on every GUI reload. Open: \\text and \\mathrm in math still use embedded sans. Checked by eye with Liberation Serif and DejaVu Math TeX Gyre.
